name: MonarchInvoiceView
title: InvoiceView
wrapsNative: VStack and Grid with LabeledContent (.monarch(.inline)), MonarchMoney and MonarchStatusBadge; printing through ImageRenderer to PDF and UIPrintInteractionController
summary: A read-only invoice: issuer and billed party, number, dates and status, billed lines, totals, notes and small print, with an optional Print button that opens the system print panel.
whenToUse: Showing an invoice that has been issued (sent, paid, overdue or cancelled), in an invoice detail screen or a client portal, and printing it or saving it as a PDF.
whenNotToUse: For many invoices, use a list of rows with MonarchMoney and MonarchStatusBadge. For a payment receipt file, use MonarchReceiptPreview. For payroll, use MonarchPayslipView. Monarch for iOS has no line items editor yet for creating invoice lines.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, number: String? = nil, status: MonarchStatusDefinition? = nil, issueDate: Date? = nil, dueDate: Date? = nil, details: [MonarchInvoiceDetail] = [], brand: Image? = nil, from: MonarchInvoiceParty? = nil, to: MonarchInvoiceParty? = nil, items: [MonarchInvoiceLineItem], currencyCode: String, locale: Locale? = nil, taxRate: Decimal? = nil, discount: MonarchInvoiceDiscount? = nil, totals: MonarchInvoiceTotals = MonarchInvoiceTotals(), notes: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, isPrintButtonShown: Bool = false, labels: MonarchInvoiceViewLabels = MonarchInvoiceViewLabels(), onPrint: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Invoice", for example "Tax invoice" or "Credit note".

options.name: number
options.description: The invoice number, shown after the title; the heading is also the invoice's accessibility name.

options.name: status
options.description: A status badge beside the title. The app owns the vocabulary ("Paid", "Overdue").

options.name: issueDate
options.description: Shown as "Issue date" with a long date in the locale and the environment's time zone.

options.name: dueDate
options.description: Shown as "Due date" with a long date.

options.name: details
options.description: Further facts after the dates, such as terms or a purchase order number.

options.name: brand
options.description: A logo above the title, scaled with the title text size. Decorative: hidden from VoiceOver.

options.name: from
options.description: Who issues the invoice, under the heading "From".

options.name: to
options.description: Who is billed, under the heading "Bill to".

options.name: items
options.description: The billed lines. Empty shows "No line items.".

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of every amount, which are in major units.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of amounts, quantities and dates. Default: the environment's.

options.name: taxRate
options.description: The tax rate in percent. Used to work out tax when totals.tax is nil, and then shown in the label ("Tax (20%)").

options.name: discount
options.description: A percentage or amount discount, used when totals.discount is nil.

options.name: totals
options.description: Totals from the billing system, shown exactly. Amount paid and amount due are shown only when given.

options.name: notes
options.description: Payment instructions or a note under the totals, with the heading "Notes".

options.name: footer
options.description: Small print at the bottom, in the caption style.

options.name: isPrintButtonShown
options.description: Shows a secondary Print button in the header (on iOS, or anywhere with onPrint).

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, for example in the invoice's own language.

options.name: onPrint
options.description: Runs instead of the built-in printing, for example to print the billing system's PDF.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra header actions after Print, such as Send or Download. Not printed.

states.name: stacked lines
states.description: At compact width and at the accessibility text sizes each line is a block: description and detail, then "Qty 2 · Unit price £400.00" and the amount.

states.name: table
states.description: At regular width the lines are a grid with Description, Qty, Unit price and Amount columns; numbers align to the trailing edge.

states.name: worked-out totals
states.description: Totals not given are worked out from the lines, the tax rate and the discount, rounded to the currency's minor unit.

states.name: given totals
states.description: Totals from the billing system are shown exactly; the tax label then has no rate.

states.name: paid and due
states.description: Amount paid and amount due rows appear after the total when given; amount due is in the strong body style.

states.name: empty
states.description: No lines shows "No line items." in muted text; the totals are zero.

states.name: printing
states.description: Print renders the invoice as A4 PDF pages in the light theme at the default text size, with the table layout and without the actions, and opens the system print panel.

appearance: The title uses the title type role in the default text colour; section headings, column headings and fact labels use the muted text colour; amounts use tabular digits. Rows are separated by dividers in the subtle border colour and the total has a divider above it and a larger type role. There are no fills apart from the status badge, so the same roles read in light, dark and both high-contrast themes, and the printed copy uses the light theme.
platformNotes: The web InvoiceView is an article with a real table and print styles, and takes ReactNode slots and decimal or minor-unit amounts. On iOS amounts are Decimal in major units, dates are Date values formatted by the view, and the status is a MonarchStatusDefinition drawn as a MonarchStatusBadge. Printing uses ImageRenderer to make PDF pages and UIPrintInteractionController, because a SwiftUI view cannot be printed directly; the system panel also offers saving as a PDF. The parity map named List sections; the view is a plain stack instead, because a List cannot sit inside a screen's ScrollView with other content and cannot be rendered to PDF. The heading level option has no iOS equivalent; headings are marked with the header trait. Android ships the same MonarchInvoiceView.
accessibility: The invoice is a container named by its heading, such as "Invoice INV-1042"; the heading has the header trait.
"From", "Bill to", "Line items" and "Notes" are headers, so the rotor can move between them.

Each line is one element read as its description and detail, then "Qty", "Unit price" and "Amount" with their values, in both layouts; the column headings are hidden because every line names its columns.
Each fact and each total is one element read as its label and then its value.
The status badge has words and an icon, so the status never depends on colour.
The brand image is decorative and hidden.
Text wraps at every Dynamic Type size; at the accessibility sizes lines stack and totals put the amount under the label.
The Print button is a MonarchButton with a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: Totals are worked out only for values left nil; a given total is never corrected, even when it disagrees with the lines.
A negative discount is ignored; a discount larger than the subtotal is capped at it.
A zero-decimal currency such as JPY rounds lines to whole units.
Dates are written in the environment's time zone; pass a date at the start of the local day for a date-only value.
Printed pages are cut at the page height, so a long invoice can split a line across two pages.
Printing and the print panel were checked by compiling for iOS and by a unit test of the PDF pages on the host; the panel was not opened on a device.

examples.title: Issued invoice, totals worked out
examples.template:
ScrollView {
    MonarchInvoiceView(
        number: {{number}},
        status: MonarchStatusDefinition({{status.label}}, tone: {{status.tone|tone}}, systemImage: "info.circle"),
        issueDate: {{issueDate|date}},
        dueDate: {{dueDate|date}},
        details: [MonarchInvoiceDetail({{detail.label}}, value: {{detail.value}})],
        from: MonarchInvoiceParty({{from.name}}, details: [{{from.details.0}}, {{from.details.1}}]),
        to: MonarchInvoiceParty({{to.name}}, details: [{{to.details.0}}]),
        items: [
            MonarchInvoiceLineItem({{items.0.id}}, description: {{items.0.description}}, detail: {{items.0.detail}}, quantity: {{items.0.quantity}}, unitPrice: {{items.0.unitPrice}}),
            MonarchInvoiceLineItem({{items.1.id}}, description: {{items.1.description}}, quantity: {{items.1.quantity}}, unitPrice: {{items.1.unitPrice}}),
            MonarchInvoiceLineItem({{items.2.id}}, description: {{items.2.description}}, detail: {{items.2.detail}}, quantity: {{items.2.quantity}}, unitPrice: {{items.2.unitPrice}}),
        ],
        currencyCode: {{currency}},
        locale: Locale(identifier: {{locale}}),
        taxRate: {{taxRate}},
        notes: {{notes}},
        isPrintButtonShown: true
    )
    .padding()
}

parityExceptions.reason: The web lays the line items out as a four column table (description, quantity, unit price, amount), which needs about 390 points; a phone column has 306, so each line stacks its description, its quantity and unit price, and its amount, with the same figures and totals. For the same reason the Print button sits under the title instead of beside it.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: a table that does not fit a compact width becomes a list of rows, not a sideways scroll
